sections.title: Early separation made softer
sections.lead: For many families, a play school in Velachery is a child’s first regular experience away from home.
points: Children can settle gradually, build trust, and join simple routines without feeling pushed.
The environment stays lively enough for engagement and calm enough for security.
Teachers give young children time to observe, warm up, and participate at their own pace.
sections.closing: First school experiences shape how children feel about learning, group spaces, and daily transitions.

sections.title: Play is the earliest learning language
sections.lead: Play is not separate from learning in the early years. It is how children discover language, movement, listening, imagination, and problem solving.
points: Children sing, speak, build, draw, move, pretend, and participate in joyful group moments.
Repeated routines and kind adults help children relax into the classroom setting.
The day encourages participation without too much noise, confusion, or pressure.
sections.closing: Rhythm and relationships help children engage more fully in a shared classroom.
